{{field-1}}" :question/worked-solution "Perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals of each other.

First, let's find the slope ${m}_{1}$ of the line passing through the points $(-1,1)$ and $(1,3):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{m}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{3-1}{1-(-1)} \\  & =\frac{3-1}{1+1} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Since we want a perpendicular line, the slope $m$ of the line we're trying to find must satisfy

$$
m\cdot (1)=-1\,⇒\,m=-1.
$$

We know that the line passes through the point $(0,1).$ Using point-slope form and simplifying, we obtain the equation of the line in slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-1 & =-1(x-0) \\ y-1 & =-x \\ y & =1 -x\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["8d9a6db0-05c1-5d85-8a67-056821eb3220"] :db/ensure :question/validate} {:db/id "generator" :question-generator/id #uuid "d4f8e14e-e664-5d3c-b8e6-ce7ab96b3db1" :question-generator/script "generate/scratch/17592186175923.py"} [:db/add 17592186175923 :knowledge-point/question-generator "generator"] {:db/id 17592186175923 :knowledge-point/questions ["e6fe3232-91eb-5c5b-90f0-5931f279e031"]} [:db/ensure 17592186175923 :knowledge-point/validate]]
